name: InputField
description: An input field lets people enter a single line of text: a name, an email address, a search term. It always has a label, and can show help text, an error or a success message, icons and a clear button.
whenToUse: To enter short free-form text: names, emails, numbers, search terms.
When the answer isn’t one of a known, short list of options.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Says what to enter. Always present; can be visually hidden for search boxes.

anatomy.name: Field
anatomy.description: The bordered box that holds the text, icons and clear button.

anatomy.name: Start icon
anatomy.description: Optional icon hinting at the content, e.g. a mail icon.

anatomy.name: Input text
anatomy.description: What the person typed, or the placeholder while empty.

anatomy.name: Help text
anatomy.description: Optional hint under the field; replaced visually by error or success.

values.meaning: Prominent single-field forms, e.g. a hero search.

states.name: Hover
states.meaning: Shows the field responds to the pointer.

states.name: Error
states.meaning: The value is missing or invalid.

states.name: Success
states.meaning: The value was checked and is valid.

states.name: Read-only
states.meaning: The value can be read and copied but not changed.

states.name: Disabled
states.meaning: The field isn’t available right now.

behavior.text: The label is required by the API. Placeholders disappear while typing, so they never replace a label.
Show errors after the person leaves the field or submits, not on every keystroke. The error text is announced with the field.
With clearable, a clear button appears while the controlled value isn’t empty; it calls onClear and returns focus to the field.
Use the right type (email, tel, url, search, number) so phones show the matching keyboard.
Icons and padding use logical sides, so the start icon sits on the right in Arabic.

content: Labels are short nouns in sentence case: "Email address", not "Enter your email address:".
Use placeholders for examples of the format ("name@company.com"), never for instructions people need later.
Write errors that say how to fix the problem: "Enter an email address like name@company.com".
Mark optional fields "(optional)" when most fields are required, or required fields with * when most are optional.

guidelines.do: Always give the field a label.
guidelines.dont: Use the placeholder as the only label.
guidelines.why: Placeholders vanish while typing and are not reliably announced.

guidelines.do: Explain how to fix an error in words.
guidelines.why: Color alone is missed by people with color blindness and by screen readers.

guidelines.do: Match the field width to the expected answer, e.g. short for a postal code.
guidelines.dont: Stretch every field to the full width regardless of content.
guidelines.why: Width hints at the expected length and makes forms easier to scan.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to and from the field (and to the clear button).

aria.when: Set automatically when there is an error.
Links the help text and the error or success message.

accessibility.focus: The whole field shows the brand border and a focus ring while typing.

wcag.how: Label, help text and messages are programmatically tied to the input.
Text, placeholder and messages pass 4.5:1 in every theme.
The field border keeps 3:1 against the background.
Errors are described in text and announced.
Every field has a label; the API requires it.

notes: A visually hidden label is still announced; use hideLabel only when the purpose is obvious, e.g. search with a search icon.

examples.title: Labelled field
examples.description: A controlled field with help text.

examples.title: Validation error
examples.description: Say how to fix the problem.

examples.title: Search with clear button
examples.description: A search box with a hidden label, icon and clear button.

related.relation: Use to choose from known options.
Wraps other controls with the same label and message layout.

changes: New optional prop: “(optional)” after the label, matching FormField and Textarea.
Required label (with hideLabel), help text, error and success messages, required marker.
Sizes, iconStart/iconEnd (replacing icon/prefix), clear button, read-only style.
Typed text uses the primary text color; the border meets 3:1; keyboard focus ring.

components.name: InputField
components.description: A single-line text field with a label and optional help, error or success message.

label.description: What to enter, e.g. "Email address". Always required: it is the field's accessible name.

hideLabel.description:
Hides the label visually but keeps it for screen readers. Only for fields whose purpose
is obvious from context, such as a search box with a search icon.

optional.description: Marks the field optional with text after the label. Use when most fields are required.

optionalLabel.description: Text shown for optional fields. Default "(optional)".

description.description: Help text under the field, e.g. format hints.

error.description: Error message. Marks the field invalid and replaces the success message.

size.description: `small` for dense UI, `medium` by default, `large` for prominent forms.

iconStart.description: Icon before the text, e.g. a search or mail icon. Hidden from screen readers.

iconEnd.description: Icon after the text. Hidden from screen readers.

clearable.description: Shows a clear button while the (controlled) value isn't empty. Use with onClear.

onClear.description: Called when the clear button is pressed; set the value to '' here.

clearLabel.description: Accessible name of the clear button. Default "Clear".
